synopsis: ISO 19014-4 supplies the off-road safety-related software and data/signal-transmission basis, requiring systematic development and verification for a brake-commanding collision-avoidance function [f2700, f2339, f12180]. As of 1 October 2026, the published edition remained 2020, while Edition 2 had reached stage 60.00 on 22 August 2026 and was scheduled for October 2026 publication; Chapter 10's DIS-stage description is therefore in tension with the later status reported elsewhere [f2325, f2326, f7737]. The final revised texts were unavailable for review, so the booklet recommends an immediate gap analysis against the second editions of Parts 1 and 4 rather than assuming their requirements are settled [f2862, f10541]. The 2020 edition contains normative Annex B on software validation test environments, supporting the recommendation to map each requirement to simulation, hardware-in-the-loop or machine testing [f10532, f12181, f10542]. Although simulation tool confidence is associated with ISO 19014-4 software verification and validation, the research did not establish whether the standard itself requires tool qualification [f8035, f10545, f11191]. Cybersecurity is explicitly outside both the cited 2020 scope and the second-edition abstract, so brake-command networks and sensor/data interfaces need separate security treatment; functional safety must not be assumed to cover it [f10354, f10534, f5832, f11268].
